hook.line: Hosts in Colombia will offer you a choice every five minutes. Here's how to ask one, and how to answer it without a speech.
hook.en: —Would you rather have black coffee or juice? —Juice, thanks.

examples.en: Do you prefer the cinema or football?

examples.es: ¿Cuál prefieres, el jugo de fruta o el chocolate?
examples.en: Which one do you prefer, the fruit juice or the hot chocolate?

rule:
Preferir is a boot verb: prefiero, prefieres, prefiere, preferimos, prefieren.

To offer a choice, name both things with o in the middle: ¿Prefieres tinto o jugo? Among friends you can drop the verb: ¿Tinto o jugo?

To answer, just pick one. Jugo, gracias is a full, polite answer. If you want a sentence: Prefiero el jugo.

Prefiero can be followed by a thing (Prefiero el cine) or by an action (Prefiero caminar).

When the two things are already on the table, ask with cuál: ¿Cuál prefieres? = Which one do you prefer?

Don't mind? Say me da igual.
smallPrint: Preferir is an e→ie stem-changing verb. ¿Cuál…? asks for a choice from a set; ¿Qué…? is more open.

readAndPick.es: Los clientes prefieren el café de Vale.

options: Do you all prefer pizza or fruit?
Do you prefer pizza or fruit? (one friend)
Do we prefer pizza or fruit?

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: beer or juice? Use preferir.
yourTurn.why: Prefieres is the tú form of the boot verb: e becomes ie.

yourTurn.prompt: Answer: you'd rather have juice. Keep it short.
yourTurn.why: Naming the thing you want is a complete answer.
Prefiero can go straight before an action.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend which one they prefer.
yourTurn.why: When the options are already in front of you, ask with cuál.
Nosotros is outside the boot: preferimos keeps the e.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a stranger politely: cinema or football?
yourTurn.why: Usted takes the él/ella form: prefiere.

yourTurn.prompt: Someone asks ¿Pizza o fruta? Say you don't mind.
yourTurn.why: Me da igual is the easy way out of any either-or question.

pitfalls.why: Preferir is a boot verb: prefiero.
Nosotros is outside the boot, and it's an -ir verb: preferimos.
An either-or question wants one of the two, not yes.

personal: Pick a side: cinema or football, beer or juice, Saturday or Sunday? Write three answers that start with Prefiero…
